record.paper_title: Understanding Solar Flares and Energetic Events: Open questions, observational requirements, and instrumental needs over the coming decade
record.original_question: Can spectral and imaging observations of solar flares be incorporated into flare-forecasting methods, particularly to infer the build-up of turbulence before a flare, and how should that spectral information flow through a research-to-operations-to-research pipeline to improve forecasting skill?

evidence.quote: • Can we use spectral and imaging observations from solar ﬂares to inform or develop ﬂare forecasting, for inferring the build of up turbulence prior to a ﬂare [23]. Including spectral information in the research-to-operations-to-research pipeline is likely fruitful [83, 84].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of forecasting solar flares, i.e., predicting the occurrence, timing, and magnitude of impulsive energy-release events in the solar atmosphere. Suppose one has access to two classes of observational data of active regions on the Sun:

1. Imaging observations: time-resolved two-dimensional intensity maps in selected wavelengths (e.g., extreme ultraviolet, soft X-ray, optical continuum, and chromospheric lines), which reveal the morphology and dynamical evolution of magnetic structures.
2. Spectral observations: spatially resolved line profiles (intensity as a function of wavelength) in chromospheric and transition-region diagnostic lines, from which line broadening beyond thermal and instrumental contributions — commonly attributed to unresolved nonthermal motions or turbulence — can be extracted as a function of position and time.

Define a "pre-flare turbulence build-up signature" as a statistically significant temporal increase, prior to the flare onset, in the nonthermal broadening component of selected spectral lines integrated over a flaring region.

Address the following:

(a) Construct, or prove the impossibility of, a forecasting scheme that takes as input the joint spectral-and-imaging time series of an active region and outputs a probability of flare occurrence within a specified future time window, such that the inclusion of pre-flare turbulence build-up signatures yields a statistically significant improvement in forecast skill (as measured by standard verification metrics such as the Brier skill score, the true skill statistic, or the Heidke skill score) over forecasts using imaging-only or magnetogram-only inputs.

(b) Specify a research-to-operations-to-research feedback architecture in which spectral diagnostics are continuously assimilated into operational forecasts and operational outcomes are fed back to refine the spectral diagnostics, and quantify the conditions on data latency, spectral cadence, spatial coverage, and signal-to-noise under which such a pipeline demonstrably improves forecasting skill relative to current operational baselines.
artifact.status_search_result: Operational solar flare forecasting currently relies primarily on photospheric magnetogram features and active-region imaging; incorporation of chromospheric/transition-region spectral diagnostics (in particular nonthermal line broadening as a turbulence proxy) into forecasting pipelines remains an active research direction with no established operational system. Recent literature highlights pre-flare nonthermal broadening as a candidate precursor but does not demonstrate an operational R2O2R pipeline using such spectral information, indicating the question is open.

status_evidence.title: Pre-flare nonthermal broadening studies (IRIS)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies report enhanced nonthermal velocities in chromospheric/TR lines prior to flares, suggested as turbulence precursors, but not yet integrated into operational forecasts.
status_evidence.claim: Pre-flare turbulence signatures are observed but not yet operationalized.

status_evidence.title: NOAA SWPC Flare Forecasting
status_evidence.snippet: Operational flare forecasts use magnetogram-based active-region classifications, not spectral line broadening diagnostics.
status_evidence.claim: Current operational forecasting does not yet incorporate spectral diagnostics.
